{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|Don't you have some kind of operating systems program that orders you to attempt to preserve the lives of intelligent beings whenever you can?"<br />"Yes, sir, that programming is included with all astromech droids. For a droid to deliberately harm or fail to prevent harm to a sentient being, its operating system module must be altered.|Han Solo and an R2-series astromech droid|<ref name="tps">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref>}}
'''Life preservation programming''', or '''LPP''', was a deeply-embedded series of commands required by law for every [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufactured in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] and later in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

LPP subroutines functioned as a final stop against behavior that would lead to harming an organic. LPP functioned independently of [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolts]] or other additional devices. They were not a 100 percent effective safeguard, but the probability of a droid going rogue was greatly lessened with enough sophisticated LPP. Manufacturing or selling a droid without life preservation programming was illegal without special government dispensation, but enforcement was lax in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].

In order to pursue a career as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], a rogue [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], required the removal of his LPP subroutines. [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] technicians eradicated this programming at the behest of the droid, and 4-LOM was integrated into Jabba's [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]], fully capable of harming and killing [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings.<ref name="OFC56">{{FigurineCite|56|Droids}}''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Although the subroutines are not explicitly spelled out in the source material, LPP is the rough equivalent of [[Wikipedia:Isaac Asimov|Isaac Asimov's]] [[Wikipedia:Three Laws of Robotics|Three Laws of Robotics]], the first of which prevents robots from harming or allowing, by inaction, harm to come to a human being.
